mcat_description.short: A prefabricated structure with a steel frame (light gauge steel or mild steel sections) and sheet/panel cladding, factory-manufactured and site-assembled for residential, commercial, or temporary accommodation use.
mcat_description.long: Steel House refers to a factory-built, site-assembled prefabricated structure whose primary load-bearing skeleton is a steel frame — either Light Gauge Steel Frame (LGSF) or conventional mild steel sections — clad with colour-coated GI sheets, PUF sandwich panels, or cement-fibre boards. Components are manufactured off-site under controlled conditions and transported for rapid on-site assembly, delivering a complete habitable structure in 30–90 days. The structural steel used conforms to IS:800 (general steel construction code) and IS:2062 (hot-rolled structural steel), while the overall building design follows the National Building Code of India. Buyers range from individual homeowners and real estate developers to government agencies procuring labour camps, disaster-relief shelters, and institutional accommodation.

market_context: In the Indian B2B market, 'Steel House' is the dominant buyer-facing term for any prefabricated structure whose primary load-bearing frame is steel — encompassing Light Gauge Steel Frame (LGSF) systems and conventional mild steel (MS) section frames. The structural steel used conforms to IS:800 (general steel construction) and IS:2062 (hot-rolled structural steel), and the overall building must comply with the National Building Code of India (NBC). Two cladding technologies dominate: colour-coated corrugated GI/GP sheet (cost-efficient, widely used for labour camps and portable cabins) and PUF/PIR sandwich panels (thermally insulated, used for residential and premium applications). Leading Indian manufacturers include Tata Steel's Nest-In (pan-India, 26+ states), EPACK Prefab, Loom Crafts, Wedge India, Bajaj Steel Industries, and Darq India. Key buyer segments are individual homeowners, real estate developers, construction contractors (site offices and labour camps), and government agencies under PMAY and Smart City Mission. The market is growing due to government housing targets, faster construction timelines (30–90 days vs. months for conventional construction), and cost predictability. Buyers in this MCAT compare on built-up area (sq ft), frame type (LGSF vs. MS), cladding/insulation type, floor count, and certifications (IS:800, NBC, seismic zone compliance).
